standard_prerequisites.name: Existence and functoriality of the Hom objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1922-1924: all required Hom objects exist and satisfy the correct functorial properties (published Stacks lemma, cited as input).

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite limits and coproducts in C
standard_prerequisites.use: C has coproducts of any two objects and finite limits; U -> V, U -> W morphisms of simplicial sets with finite nonempty terms, degenerate in high degrees.

core_obligations: The representability chain (proof lines 1924-1940): the nth term of the left-hand side represents the functor X |-> Mor(X x Delta[n], Hom(V,T) x_Hom(U,T) Hom(W,T)), which by the functorial properties of Hom equals Mor(X x Delta[n] x V, T) fibre-product Mor(X x Delta[n] x W, T) over Mor(X x Delta[n] x U, T).
The pushout identification (lines 1941-1948): (X x Delta[n] x V) x_{X x Delta[n] x U} (X x Delta[n] x W) = X x Delta[n] x (V amalg_U W), which the author verifies term by term.
Conclusion (lines 1949-1956): the last term of the chain corresponds to Hom(V amalg_U W, T)_n, so the fibre product on the left is represented by the Hom object on the right.
proof_roadmap: Compute the nth term of the fibre product of Hom objects by the Yoneda lemma.
Use the Hom-preservation of finite limits to split the fibre product.
Identify the term-by-term pushout and conclude representability.
difficulty_reason: Representability lemma (statement 1902-1920, proof 1922-1956): shows the fibre product Hom(V,T) x_Hom(U,T) Hom(W,T) is represented by Hom(V amalg_U W, T) via a Yoneda chain of functorial equalities plus a term-by-term pushout computation; the existence of the Hom objects is cited from the published existence lemma; no verification is omitted beyond the acknowledged term-by-term check. H2: Yoneda bookkeeping with finite limits.
